narrative_purpose: Compare the launch bottleneck on two worlds: Earth's giant pterosaur needs a four-limb pole-vault from level ground, while the ikran uses a running cliff drop and Pandora's dense air and low gravity to convert the fall into flight.
subject: A matched two-world launch study. On the left, a giant Quetzalcoatlus on an open Cretaceous plain vaults from all four limbs, folded wing-fingers and powerful forelimbs pushing the body airborne like poles while the hind feet leave the ground. On the right, a mountain banshee with a Na'vi rider sprints on its limbs from a high Pandoran cliff edge, drops into open air, and begins spreading four broad flight membranes as the forest canopy falls far below.
scene: Earth's dry level floodplain and Pandora's misty cliff are joined as two adjacent environmental vignettes with a dark vertical seam.
camera: Low lateral view on the pterosaur at the instant of vault; wider three-quarter view slightly above the banshee as it crosses the cliff lip.
light: Muted warm dawn on the Earth side, cool cyan planetshine and bioluminescent haze on the Pandora side; both subjects rim-lit against open sky.
palette: Earth panel in stone grey, muted ochre, and scarce ember; Pandora panel in void indigo, ocean teal, and Pandora cyan, with restrained continuity across the seam.
style: Painterly comparative flight-biology naturalist plate, hand-painted, physical and observational rather than cinematic spectacle.
detail_level: Crisp on the pterosaur's four-limb launch posture and the banshee's unfolding four flight membranes; landscapes recede into haze.
composition: Two equal horizontal vignettes capture the decisive instant before sustained flight, with each animal moving toward central open sky and no arrows or measurements.
consistency_notes: Quetzalcoatlus launches quadrupedally with membranous wings supported by elongated fingers. The ikran retains exactly four distinct flight membranes and canonical head and body proportions.
negative_prompt: no text, no labels, no arrows, no charts, no feathered wings on pterosaur, no dragon anatomy, no extra wings or limbs, no photorealistic or glossy 3D render look, no cartoon or anime style
